instruction: Extract the 'Foreword' from the Living Planet Report 2016 PDF (wwf folder on Desktop) and create a Google Doc called 'conservation_foreword', saving it to the /wwf_materials folder on Google Drive.

metadata.explanation: Task requires extracting the 'Foreword' section from the Living Planet Report 2016 PDF and creating a Google Doc named 'conservation_foreword' in the /wwf_materials folder. The evaluator checks for key conservation-related concepts (WWF, planet, biodiversity, wildlife) with minimum length requirement. This variation uses a different source PDF (Living Planet Report instead of GE Guidebook) while maintaining similar task complexity. Custom getter extracts document text, metric validates keyword presence.

scoring_breakdown.0.7: Contains all required keywords (WWF, planet, biodiversity, wildlife)
scoring_breakdown.1.0: Title keyword 'Foreword' appears in first 500 characters

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly downloads Google Doc from path ['wwf_materials', 'conservation_foreword'] and extracts text using python-docx
Metric correctly handles expected parameter as rules dict (uses expected.get('required_keywords') directly)
Document location verification is correct - checks the required /wwf_materials folder path
Logic flow is correct: text extraction -> keyword/length validation with partial credit scoring
Runtime feasibility confirmed - uses official get_googledrive_file getter and standard python-docx library
Verification criteria are semantically weak - generic keywords (WWF, planet, biodiversity, wildlife) could match many conservation documents, not specifically the Living Planet Report 2016 Foreword
Cannot verify content authenticity - an agent could copy any conservation text with these keywords and pass, rather than extracting the actual Foreword section from the specified PDF
Title keyword check only verifies 'Foreword' appears in first 500 chars, not that it's the actual section title from the source PDF
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Add more specific keywords unique to the Living Planet Report 2016 Foreword (e.g., specific author names, unique phrases from that foreword)
Consider adding expected content patterns or quotes that are unique to the LPR 2016 Foreword to prevent false positives
Increase min_length requirement or add max_length bounds based on actual Foreword length to prevent copying entire documents
Add validation for document structure (e.g., checking if it starts with typical foreword opening patterns)
